title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 14 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Chronicles chapter 14 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 14 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Chronicles Chapter 14.

questions.question: Who sent messengers to David with timber of cedars and craftsmen to build him a house?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 14:1 states that Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David with timber of cedars and craftsmen to build him a house.

questions.question: What did David perceive about the LORD's confirmation over him?
options: The LORD had confirmed him king over Israel
The LORD was angry with him
The LORD had chosen another king
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD had confirmed him king over Israel
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 14:2 explains that David perceived the LORD had confirmed him king over Israel because his kingdom was lifted up on high.

questions.question: Where did David take more wives?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 14:3 tells us that David took more wives at Jerusalem.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT listed as one of David's sons in Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 14:4 lists David's sons as Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon, but Absalom is not mentioned here.

questions.question: Which son of David is named in 1 Chronicles 14:5?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 14:5 mentions Ibhar as one of David's sons.

questions.question: Which of the following is a son of David according to 1 Chronicles 14:6?
questions.explanation: Nepheg is listed among the sons of David in 1 Chronicles 14:6.

questions.question: True or False: Hiram king of Tyre sent gold and silver along with timber and craftsmen to build David's house.
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 14:1 only mentions timber of cedars, masons, and carpenters sent by Hiram, not gold or silver.

questions.question: True or False: David's kingdom was lifted up on high because of the people of Israel.
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 14:2 states David's kingdom was lifted up on high because of his people Israel.

questions.question: Which of these sons of David is mentioned first in 1 Chronicles 14:4?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 14:4 lists Shammua first among David's sons in Jerusalem.

questions.question: How many sons of David are named in 1 Chronicles 14:4-7?
questions.explanation: Counting the names in 1 Chronicles 14:4-7 yields 13 sons of David mentioned.

questions.question: True or False: David's wives and children were all born in Hebron.
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 14:3 and 14:4 specify David took more wives and begat children in Jerusalem, not Hebron.

questions.question: After hearing the Philistines sought to attack, what did David do?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 14:8 says David heard and went out against the Philistines.

questions.question: Where did the Philistines spread themselves to seek David?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 14:9 states the Philistines spread themselves in the valley of Rephaim.

questions.question: What was David's first action before going into battle against the Philistines?
options: He sent messengers to the Philistines
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 14:10 shows that David enquired of God whether he should go up against the Philistines.

questions.question: In 1 Chronicles 14, which event comes first?
options: David receiving help from Hiram king of Tyre
David enquiring of God before battle
questions.correctAnswer: David receiving help from Hiram king of Tyre
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 14:1 records Hiram's help first, then David took more wives (verse 3), then battles occur later in the chapter.

medium.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 14 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Chronicles Chapter 14 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Who were some of the children of David born in Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 14:4 lists David's children in Jerusalem, including Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon, distinguishing them from other names or biblical figures.

questions.question: What did David perceive about his kingdom after Hiram king of Tyre sent him timber and workers?
options: That the LORD had confirmed him king over Israel
That his kingdom would soon fall
That he needed to conquer more lands
That he should build a palace immediately
questions.correctAnswer: That the LORD had confirmed him king over Israel
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 14:2 explains that David perceived the LORD had confirmed him king because his kingdom was lifted up on high because of Israel.

questions.question: What was the Philistines' reaction when they heard David was anointed king over all Israel?
options: All the Philistines went up to seek David
questions.correctAnswer: All the Philistines went up to seek David
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 14:8 states that when the Philistines heard David was king over all Israel, they went up to seek him, indicating their hostile intent.

questions.question: Where did the Philistines spread themselves when they came to face David?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 14:9 specifies that the Philistines spread themselves out in the valley of Rephaim, setting the stage for the battle with David.

questions.question: What question did David ask God before going to battle against the Philistines?
options: "Shall I go up against the Philistines? and wilt thou deliver them into mine hand?"
"Should I make peace with the Philistines?"
questions.correctAnswer: "Shall I go up against the Philistines? and wilt thou deliver them into mine hand?"
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 14:10 records David inquiring of God whether he should go up against the Philistines and if God would deliver them into his hands, showing David's reliance on divine guidance.

questions.question: What was the name of the place where David smote the Philistines and why was it called that?
options: Baalperazim, because God broke in upon the enemies like the breaking forth of waters
Gibeon, because of the great battle there
Ziklag, named for the nearby river
questions.correctAnswer: Baalperazim, because God broke in upon the enemies like the breaking forth of waters
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 14:11 explains that the battle took place at Baalperazim, named by David because God had broken in upon his enemies like a flood of water.

questions.question: What did David command to be done with the gods the Philistines left behind?
options: They were returned to the Philistines
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 14:12 states that after the Philistines left their gods, David commanded they be burned with fire, signifying the rejection of false gods.

questions.question: How did God instruct David to respond when the Philistines spread themselves abroad again in the valley?
options: Go not up after them; turn away and come upon them over against the mulberry trees
questions.correctAnswer: Go not up after them; turn away and come upon them over against the mulberry trees
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 14:14 records God's command to David to avoid a direct pursuit and instead come upon the Philistines near the mulberry trees, showing divine strategy in battle.

questions.question: What sign did God tell David to wait for before going out to battle the second time?
options: The sound of going in the tops of the mulberry trees
questions.correctAnswer: The sound of going in the tops of the mulberry trees
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 14:15 instructs David to wait for the sound of movement in the mulberry trees before attacking, indicating God's presence going before him.

questions.question: What was the outcome when David obeyed God's command regarding the second battle with the Philistines?
options: They smote the host of the Philistines from Gibeon even to Gazer
The Philistines fled without a fight
They made a treaty with the Philistines
questions.correctAnswer: They smote the host of the Philistines from Gibeon even to Gazer
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 14:16 describes the victory David achieved by following God's instructions, defeating the Philistine army across a broad region.

questions.question: What effect did David's victories and reputation have on other nations?
options: The LORD brought the fear of him upon all nations
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD brought the fear of him upon all nations
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 14:17 states that David's fame spread and God caused all nations to fear him, showing God's blessing on David's leadership.

questions.question: How does 1 Chronicles 14 teach about the importance of seeking God's guidance before making decisions?
options: David enquired of God both times before battle, receiving clear instructions
David acted impulsively without consulting God
David asked his generals instead of God
David relied solely on his own strength
questions.correctAnswer: David enquired of God both times before battle, receiving clear instructions
questions.explanation: Verses 10 and 14 show David repeatedly seeking God's direction before engaging the Philistines, illustrating faith and dependence on God for guidance.

questions.question: True or False: David's victory over the Philistines was solely due to his military strategy without any divine intervention.
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 14:10-16 shows that David's victories were achieved by obeying God's commands, with God going before him to defeat the Philistines.

questions.question: True or False: After the first battle at Baalperazim, David burned the Philistines' gods to demonstrate rejection of idolatry.
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 14:12 clearly states that David commanded the gods left by the Philistines to be burned, rejecting their idolatry.

questions.question: True or False: The name Baalperazim means that the place was named after a Philistine god.
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 14:11 explains Baalperazim was named by David because God broke in upon the enemies like bursting waters, not after a Philistine deity.

hard.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 14 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Chronicles Chapter 14.

questions.question: What specific instruction did God give David about how to approach the Philistines when they spread abroad again in the valley?
options: Turn away from them and come upon them over against the mulberry trees
Wait until they leave the valley
questions.correctAnswer: Turn away from them and come upon them over against the mulberry trees
questions.explanation: God instructed David to not pursue the Philistines directly but to turn away and attack them near the mulberry trees, as stated in 1 Chronicles 14:14.

questions.question: What was the sign David was to wait for before going out to battle against the Philistines near the mulberry trees?
options: The sound of going in the tops of the mulberry trees
questions.correctAnswer: The sound of going in the tops of the mulberry trees
questions.explanation: David was told to wait for the sound of movement in the tops of the mulberry trees as a signal to attack, according to 1 Chronicles 14:15.

questions.question: From where to where did David smite the host of the Philistines after following God's command?
questions.explanation: David defeated the Philistines from Gibeon to Gazer as a result of obeying God's command, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 14:16.

questions.question: What was the effect on the nations because of the fame of David and the LORD's actions?
options: The LORD brought the fear of David upon all nations
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD brought the fear of David upon all nations
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 14:17 explains that the fame of David spread widely and the LORD caused all nations to fear him.

questions.question: What does the name Baalperazim, the place where David first defeated the Philistines, mean in the context of the battle?
questions.explanation: David named the place Baalperazim meaning 'The Lord has broken forth' because God broke through his enemies like water, as stated in 1 Chronicles 14:11.

questions.question: What did David do with the gods the Philistines left behind after their defeat?
options: He placed them in the temple
He returned them to the Philistines
He hid them in a cave
questions.explanation: David commanded that the idols the Philistines left behind be burned with fire, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 14:12.

questions.question: Which king sent messengers to David with cedar timber and skilled workers to build him a house?
questions.explanation: Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David with cedar timber and craftsmen to build David a house, as described in 1 Chronicles 14:1.

questions.question: According to 1 Chronicles 14, what was David's perception about the LORD's confirmation of his kingship?
options: That he would be king for only a short time
That the LORD had confirmed him king over Israel because his kingdom was exalted on high for his people
That he needed to conquer more lands to be confirmed
That his kingdom depended on military strength alone
questions.correctAnswer: That the LORD had confirmed him king over Israel because his kingdom was exalted on high for his people
questions.explanation: David perceived that the LORD confirmed him king because his kingdom was lifted high on account of his people Israel, as stated in 1 Chronicles 14:2.

questions.question: Which of the following was NOT one of David’s sons born in Jerusalem mentioned in this chapter?
questions.explanation: Absalom is not listed among David's sons in 1 Chronicles 14; the sons mentioned are Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon, Ibhar, Elishua, Elpalet, Nogah, Nepheg, Japhia, Elishama, Beeliada, and Eliphalet (1 Chronicles 14:4-7).

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is thematically connected to David’s inquiry of God before battle in 1 Chronicles 14?
options: Exodus 14:15-16 where Moses parts the Red Sea
1 Samuel 23:2 where David enquires of the LORD about attacking the Philistines
Psalm 23 where David speaks of the Lord as shepherd
questions.correctAnswer: 1 Samuel 23:2 where David enquires of the LORD about attacking the Philistines
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 23:2 parallels 1 Chronicles 14:10 where David asks God if he should attack the Philistines, showing a consistent theme of seeking divine guidance before battle.

questions.question: What literary device is exemplified by the repeated seeking of God's guidance before each battle in this chapter?
questions.explanation: The repeated inquiries to God before battles (verses 10 and 14) display parallelism, emphasizing dependence on divine guidance.

questions.question: What is the significance of the Hebrew word 'Baalperazim' as used in this chapter?
questions.explanation: The name Baalperazim means 'The Lord who breaks through,' referring to God's intervention in breaking David’s enemies like water, as explained in 1 Chronicles 14:11.

questions.question: True or False: David built the house for himself using only Israelite laborers without any foreign assistance.
questions.explanation: Hiram king of Tyre sent cedars, masons, and carpenters to help David build his house, indicating foreign assistance (1 Chronicles 14:1).

questions.question: True or False: David's fame and the fear he inspired among nations was solely due to his military conquests without any acknowledgment of the LORD's intervention.
questions.explanation: David’s fame and the fear of him among nations were attributed to the LORD’s actions as well as his victories (1 Chronicles 14:17).

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God going before His people to fight their battles as seen in 1 Chronicles 14:15?
options: Romans 8:31 - If God be for us, who can be against us?
Philippians 4:13 - I can do all things through Christ
Hebrews 11:1 - Faith is the substance of things hoped for
Ephesians 6:11 - Put on the whole armor of God
questions.correctAnswer: Romans 8:31 - If God be for us, who can be against us?
questions.explanation: Romans 8:31 reflects the assurance that God fights on behalf of His people, paralleling 1 Chronicles 14:15 where God goes before David to smite his enemies.

theological.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 14 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Chronicles Chapter 14 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does David's receipt of cedar timber and skilled workers from Hiram king of Tyre reveal about the nature of his kingdom?
options: David's kingdom was recognized and supported by foreign rulers
David was dependent on foreign aid for survival
David was forced into alliances due to military weakness
David's kingdom was isolated from neighboring nations
questions.correctAnswer: David's kingdom was recognized and supported by foreign rulers
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 14:1 shows that Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers with timber and skilled workers to build David a house, indicating international recognition and support of David's kingdom. This reflects God's confirmation of David's reign and foreshadows the future temple building.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is primarily demonstrated when God confirms David as king and lifts his kingdom because of Israel?
options: Immutability in keeping promises to David
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 14:2 says David perceived that the LORD had confirmed him king over Israel and lifted up his kingdom, demonstrating God's omnipotence in sovereignly establishing David’s reign.

questions.question: What theological significance can be drawn from David taking more wives and fathering more children in Jerusalem?
options: It reflects God's blessing of fruitfulness and dynastic continuation
It shows David's failure to remain faithful to one wife
It indicates political alliances through marriage
questions.correctAnswer: It reflects God's blessing of fruitfulness and dynastic continuation
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 14:3 shows David taking more wives and fathering children, which in the biblical context symbolizes God's blessing of fruitfulness and establishment of David’s dynastic line, crucial for messianic fulfillment.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of David's sons mentioned in this chapter?
questions.explanation: Verses 4-7 list David's sons as Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon, Ibhar, Elishua, Elpalet, Nogah, Nepheg, Japhia, Elishama, Beeliada, and Eliphalet. Jonathan is not mentioned as David's son here.

questions.question: How does David's inquiry of God before battle illustrate the doctrine of divine providence?
options: It shows that God directs the affairs of nations and battles
It reveals that David doubted God's power
It indicates that human effort alone secures victory
It implies fate controls the outcomes, not God
questions.correctAnswer: It shows that God directs the affairs of nations and battles
questions.explanation: In 1 Chronicles 14:10, David enquires of God whether to go up against the Philistines and God directs him to go, demonstrating divine providence as God sovereignly governs the outcomes of human events.

questions.question: What attribute of God is revealed in His promise to deliver David's enemies into his hand?
questions.explanation: God's assurance to David in 1 Chronicles 14:10 that He will deliver the Philistines into his hand evidences God's faithfulness to fulfill His promises to His servant.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth is expressed by the naming of the place Baalperazim after God's intervention?
options: God's power to break the strength of enemies
The futility of trusting in pagan gods
The necessity of human military strategy
questions.correctAnswer: God's power to break the strength of enemies
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 14:11 recounts David naming the place Baalperazim, meaning 'Lord of Breakings,' signifying God's power to break David's enemies' resistance as waters break forth.

questions.question: How does David’s command to burn the Philistines' idols relate to Israel’s doctrine of holiness and idolatry?
options: It enforces the exclusivity of worship of Yahweh
It tolerates other gods as cultural expressions
It shows syncretism between Israelite and Philistine religion
It reveals a political strategy rather than religious concern
questions.correctAnswer: It enforces the exclusivity of worship of Yahweh
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 14:12 describes David commanding the idols left by the Philistines to be burned, demonstrating Israel’s doctrine that worship must be exclusive to Yahweh and idolatry must be abolished.

questions.question: What combined theological insight about God’s guidance and warfare can be drawn from verses 14 and 15?
options: God provides strategic guidance and divine initiative in battle
God expects Israel to fight independently of His will
Human wisdom is superior to divine instruction
Victory depends on surprise tactics alone
questions.correctAnswer: God provides strategic guidance and divine initiative in battle
questions.explanation: Verses 14-15 show God instructing David not to pursue the Philistines directly but to wait for a sign (sound in the mulberry trees), emphasizing God’s active guidance and initiative in securing victory.

questions.question: How does David’s obedience to God's commands in battle exemplify sanctification in the life of a believer?
options: It demonstrates submission to God's will as a process of growth
It indicates human effort alone leads to holiness
It shows perfection in human obedience
It suggests sanctification is irrelevant to leadership
questions.correctAnswer: It demonstrates submission to God's will as a process of growth
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 14:16 reveals David doing as God commanded, illustrating sanctification as continual submission to God’s will, leading to spiritual growth and victorious living.

questions.question: In what way does the widespread fame of David and the fear of him among nations reflect God's providential plan for Israel?
options: It shows God's use of David's reign to establish His kingdom among nations
It indicates David's political dominance without divine involvement
It reflects Israel's isolation from international affairs
It suggests fear was based solely on military power
questions.correctAnswer: It shows God's use of David's reign to establish His kingdom among nations
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 14:17 states that the fame of David spread and the LORD caused fear of him among all nations, indicating God’s providential work through David to prepare Israel for messianic kingdom purposes (cf. Psalm 2:8-9).

questions.question: Sceptics claim that biblical accounts of divine intervention in battles are mere myth. What does 1 Chronicles 14:10-16 actually teach about God's involvement in historical events?
options: God actively directs and enables victory for His chosen king
God is indifferent to human conflicts
Human might alone determines battle outcomes
The text is symbolic with no historical basis
questions.correctAnswer: God actively directs and enables victory for His chosen king
questions.explanation: Verses 10-16 record David enquiring of God and receiving specific instructions, which he obeys resulting in victory, teaching God’s providential and active involvement in history, countering sceptical claims.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching about God's justice and holiness is seen in the defeat of the Philistines and destruction of their idols in verses 11 and 12?
options: God executes righteous judgment against idolatry and enemies
God tolerates pagan practices within Israel
God's justice is delayed and uncertain
God's holiness allows idolatry to coexist
questions.correctAnswer: God executes righteous judgment against idolatry and enemies
questions.explanation: Verses 11 and 12 together show God breaking David’s enemies and commanding the burning of their idols, illustrating God’s justice in judging both the Philistines and their idolatry, underscoring His holiness.

questions.question: How do verses 4-7 and verse 17 together contribute to the biblical theology of the Davidic covenant and messianic hope?
options: They establish David’s royal lineage and God's universal exaltation of his throne
They focus solely on David's military exploits
They deny any future significance of David's descendants
They emphasize human effort over divine promise
questions.correctAnswer: They establish David’s royal lineage and God's universal exaltation of his throne
questions.explanation: Verses 4-7 list David’s sons, establishing his royal lineage, while verse 17 shows God spreading David’s fame and fear among nations, together underscoring the Davidic covenant’s messianic hope (cf. 2 Samuel 7).

questions.question: What theological insight about human dependence on God can be synthesized from David’s multiple inquiries before battle in verses 10 and 14?
options: Faith requires continual seeking of God's will in decisions
Prayer is unnecessary once victory is assured
Human planning is superior to divine guidance
God’s will is unknowable and irrelevant
questions.correctAnswer: Faith requires continual seeking of God's will in decisions
questions.explanation: David enquires of God twice before battle (verses 10 and 14), showing that living by faith involves ongoing dependence on God's guidance for decisions, highlighting the believer’s sanctification process.
